The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 & 2 : In the Negative Point No.3 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 & 2: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined CW1 by name Smt Gayathri, being informant as PW1 who deposed that on 16.05.2016, she got married with the Accused, at the time, she had given gold to him, after marriage, accused started ill treating her, later she had begotten one baby girl, however the accused used to suspect her character and asked her to undergo DNA Test about the paternity of child, after 3 months of compromise, accused repeated the harassment, he does not want baby girl and beaten her daughter and forced her to put signature as he wanted to get second marriage,
therefore, she filed complaint as per Ex.P1, police conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 in presence of CW2 and CW3, at the time she furnished marriage invitation card, 4 photos and rental agreement as per Ex.P3 to Ex.P5 15.
Evidence of Prosecution must be established that the accused persons subjected the PW1 to mental and physical cruelty.

Mere omnibus statement regarding harassment does not ipso facto makes out a case under section 498A IPC, prosecution is required to prove the overt acts attributed by the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt and the said principle is appreciated in case of Sakharam and another vs State of Maharastra reported in (2003) 12 SCC 368.

Basing this decision,
the present cases are taken up for discussion.
16. It is relevant to reiterate Section 498A of Indian Penal Code which reads as under Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty --

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

-- For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

For commission of an offence under Section 498- A of IPC, the following necessary ingredients require to be satisfied:

sentences.text: Every harassment does not amount to "cruelty" within the meaning of Section 498-A.

For the purpose of Section 498-A, harassment simpliciter is not "cruelty" and it is only when harassment is committed for the purpose of coercing a woman or any other person related to her to meet an unlawful demand for property, etc. that it amounts to "cruelty" punishable under Section 498-A IPC and the said principle is appreciated in the case of State of A.P. vs.

M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582.
18.
Cruelty can either be mental or physical.
It is difficult for straitjacket the term cruelty by means of a definition because cruelty is a relative term.

What constitutes cruelty for one person may not constitute cruelty for another person and the said principle is appreciated in the case of G.V.
Siddaramesh v. State of Karnataka

Though the PW1 has initially supported the prosecution case however subsequent to the evidence given, deposed in her cross examination and re-examination as under Cross-examination of PW1 It is false to suggest that, at the instigation of my mother I filed false complaint.
I have furnished the receipts in respect of purchase of gold which was given to Accused.
It is false to suggest that, I have never given any receipts before the Police.
It is false to suggest that, Accused never questioned the paternity of the child, I am deposing falsely before the Court.
It is true to suggest that, Accused had filed Petition u/s.9 of Hindu Marriage Act.
It may be true that in the same Petition Accused has claimed child belongs to him.
It is true to suggest that, in the mediation we settled our dispute, later me and my child went to his house.
Witness admitted the certified copy of MC Petition 3059/2020 and same are marked as Ex.D1 and 2.
It is false to suggest that, Accused never told me that he will bring the child from orphanage.
It is false to suggest that, Accused never assaulted physically and mentally either to me or my child.
have not produced the property documents to the Police.
It is true to suggest that, previously I filed complaint against Accused, his parents and his sister and her husband.
It is true to suggest that, the said case was closed before this Court.
It is false to suggest that, in order to take the money from Accused, I filed this false complaint.

It is false to suggest that, Accused never Hebbal Police Station vs Surya Mallesh on 23 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60756739/
5 threatened me to sign.
It is false to suggest that, police have not conducted mahazar at house.
Witness volunteers that some unknown person went to the school of my daughter and asked for her progress report and claimed himself he is taking care of her education.
I have stated same before the police.
Witness volunteers that the said happened subsequent to this case.
It is false to suggest that, to demand money I filed the false case against the Accused.
Re - examination:

    Thus, it appears from the cross examination of PW1 being informant cum victim did not support the prosecution case for coherence with the contents of complaint and chief-in-examination and earlier cross examination on account of settlement arrived in matrimonial case between the PW1 and the accused.
20.

This court is of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution case that would not helpful as PW1 herself did not support the prosecution case in the cross examination.

This court has dispensed with the examination of other witnesses which could be only formal in nature and hence taken the prosecution evidence as closed after examination of police official witnesses.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision in the case of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and another reported in (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."

Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the Point No.1 and 2 is answered in the negative.
